items.question: How many random walks per vertex did DeepWalk use when learning latent social representations, and what exact walk length did the authors choose?
items.why_unanswerable: The passage says DeepWalk uses local information from truncated random walks, but it does not report the number of walks per vertex or the walk length.
items.evidence_quote: Using local information from truncated random walks as input, our method learns a representation which encodes structural regularities.

items.question: What hidden-layer size or embedding dimensionality did DeepWalk use in its representation learning model?
items.why_unanswerable: The passage describes DeepWalk as learning a representation, but it never gives the dimensionality of the learned vectors or any hidden-layer size.
items.evidence_quote: We propose DeepW alk, a novel approach for learning latent social representations of vertices.

items.question: Under which specific graph datasets did DeepWalk outperform spectral methods, and what were the exact classification accuracy numbers on each dataset?
items.why_unanswerable: The passage mentions experiments on a variety of graphs and says DeepWalk outperforms other methods on large graphs, but it does not name the datasets or provide accuracy values.
items.evidence_quote: Experiments on a variety of different graphs illustrate the effectiveness of our approach on challenging multi-label classification tasks.

items.question: How many worker threads or machines did DeepWalk use to update different parts of the model concurrently, and what speedup did the parallelization achieve?
items.why_unanswerable: The passage states that DeepWalk is parallelizable and that workers can update different parts concurrently, but it does not specify the number of workers or any measured speedup.
items.evidence_quote: We also show that our approach is parallelizable, allowing workers to update different parts of the model concurrently.
